gen-dafont-capture-smallz-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp and heavy, a dense band of text whose letters stay held open. Supreme gives Capture Smallz, with its big-bodied raw lowercase, something solid to stand beside.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-satoshi: Eight Bit Dragon strides out wide and adventurous, its lowercase towering. Satoshi then carries a long stretch of text easily, its sans strokes cut to one width and its tall, open e never pinching shut.
gen-dafont-galaxy-work-sans: Galaxy's lowercase is dense and tall, every stroke the same width, spaced loosely. Work Sans sits beneath it with a modern, contemporary feel, its mean line set high, so the cosmic top line gets a steadier sans partner.
gen-dafont-nulshock-switzer: Stretched, technical and outlined, Nulshock spreads out with capitals barely above its lowercase. Switzer follows in wiry, tubular sans-serif letters with a tall waist line, so a long passage moves along with a friendly Swiss ease.
gen-dafont-college-manrope: College hits with authority, its curves as thick as its stems and its lowercase tall. And Manrope keeps a bright gap at each curve's mouth in a sans-serif line, so a long passage goes down smoothly.
gen-dafont-conthrax-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans makes words look sturdy and large, its tall lowercase keeping the e wide open to the right. Conthrax is best at one smooth, unmodulated geometric thread; the body font is best at weight in the words.
gen-gf-unkempt-fs-bespoke-sans: Expressive and commanding, Unkempt looks traced with a single marker, its t built from crossbar and stem of matching weight. But Bespoke Sans feels sharp and refined beside it, giving its curves generous room before the stem.
gen-gf-wallpoet-archivo: Wallpoet looks like stencil work, smooth around each bend, with high lowercase and gaps showing paper. Archivo then opens its curves outward in a sans with a commanding x-height, so a long passage reads with an editorial, friendly ease.
gen-gf-wallpoet-fs-asap: Wallpoet is stencil-cut and bold, with tall lowercase and paper showing between its letters. Wallpoet does commanding display best, while Asap does readable work, its open-arc c forms and near-capital body height suiting a sans-serif text line.
gen-gf-wallpoet-fs-epilogue: Bold and stencil-like, Wallpoet takes smooth bends and a high-rising lowercase, with paper showing through between its letters. Epilogue's wire-like sans-serif curves loosen it up and make a friendly contemporary partner.
